The first summit of Exchangeability (TauCetiRoadmap#21, TauCetiRoadmap#52) has been reached -- the forward direction of de Finetti's theorem via the reverse martingale proof of Aldous (as written in Kallenberg's book and guided by my Lean formalization)!

I think the TauCeti proof is considerably cleaner and more reusable than the guide formalization. Congratulations to TauCeti and thanks to everyone for roadmap review and for contributing PRs and review bots to the formalization.

See TauCeti#801 for details of how it finished and TauCeti#856 for an update on what other things remain from the roadmap (quite a bit, though it'll be a while before another summit as prominent).

Here are some summary statistics:

Directory Files LOC Commits
Probability/Exchangeability/ 22 2,965 33
Probability/DeFinetti/ 8 1,171 11
Probability/Martingale/ 6 907 8
Probability/Process/ (Tail.lean) 1 269 7
MeasureTheory/Measure/ProductKernel.lean 1 156 3
Probability/Ergodic/ (ShiftInvariantSigma) 1 118 1
Total 39 5,586 56 (distinct union)
Awesome! In what ways is the TauCeti proof cleaner than the guide formalization?

I'm in the process of putting together a more detailed report, but I think the biggest gains have come from

  1. using mathlib even more (especially re martingales and π-systems),
  2. generalizing statements where possible (e.g., to use [StandardBorelSpace α] rather than [StandardBorelSpace Ω] or avoiding unnecessary hypotheses like weakening [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] to [IsFiniteMeasure μ]),
  3. cleaner interfaces and division between private/public and more idiomatic naming, and
  4. better automation via helper lemmas tagged for simp or grind.

Here are some more details gathered from mining the repo.
:robot: drafted with Opus 4.8, revised in light of critique from GPT 5.5

Where TauCeti's de Finetti formalization came out cleaner than cameronfreer/exchangeability

A survey of the ~56 PRs that built the Exchangeability / de Finetti area (Probability/Exchangeability, Probability/DeFinetti, Probability/Martingale, Probability/Ergodic, Probability/Process, MeasureTheory/Measure/ProductKernel), against the migration source cameronfreer/exchangeability at the cited pin e0532e59.

The most prominent ways TauCeti came out cleaner

1. Consume Mathlib characterisations instead of hand-rolled π-systems

The clearest genuine simplifications, verifiable as line reductions:

  • TauCeti#567 — Contractable.pairLaw_eq is ~46 Lean lines (Contractability.lean:219), with no cylinders and no π-system, in place of the source's rectangle π-system apparatus: PairLawEquality.lean (556 LOC) + FutureRectangles.lean (385 LOC) at the pin. (The "~55 lines / ~525 LOC" in the first draft were the PR's own merge-time self-counts; the file-level counts above are the concrete ones.)
  • Mathlib's iCondIndepFun_iff_condExp_inter_preimage_eq_mul / condIndep_iff instead of a hand-built π-system (TauCeti#658, TauCeti#760); IsProjectiveLimit.unique instead of a new cylinder / π-system proof (TauCeti#482); no new ProductKernel structure — the lemmas live directly over Mathlib's ProbabilityMeasure.pi (TauCeti#501).

2. Re-route the directing-measure endpoint through the tower; re-shape reverse martingales as Mathlib adapters

This is an honest re-architecture, not a net line reduction.

  • TauCeti#579 (93 LOC added) proves Contractable.condExp_indicator_tailProcess_eq via the plain Mathlib tower condExp_condExp_of_le (DeFinetti/CondExpConvergence.lean:56), so the directing-measure coordinate-law endpoint carries no reverse-martingale dependency. The source already had a tower alternative (extreme_members_equal_on_tail_via_tower, source DeFinetti/ViaMartingale/CondExpConvergence.lean:84), but its directing-measure theorem used the reverse-martingale route (extreme_members_equal_on_tail, source DeFinetti/ViaMartingale/DirectingMeasure.lean:137). TauCeti's win is making the cleaner tower route — routed through Contractable.pairLaw_eq — the actual dependency of the endpoint.
  • Separately, TauCeti deliberately reintroduced a reverse-martingale layer — 907 LOC (Reverse 83, Convergence 116, AntitoneLimit 106, Crossings/Bounds 247, Crossings/Pathwise 189, Crossings/TimeReversal 166) — for tail-level factorization (consumed at DeFinetti/TailFactorization.lean:69), built as thin adapters over Mathlib's upcrossing + convergence API: TauCeti#685, TauCeti#686, TauCeti#724, TauCeti#734, TauCeti#743, TauCeti#755; helper PRs TauCeti#687 / TauCeti#772; consumer TauCeti#790.
  • Net picture: at the pin, the source's generic reverse-martingale machinery is ~957 LOC (≈1,163 including TimeReversalCrossing.lean), rising to ~1,387–1,593 with its de-Finetti-specific FutureFiltration / RevFiltration / KallenbergChain. TauCeti re-architected this into a smaller (~907 LOC), Mathlib-shaped adapter layer plus the tower short-circuit for the coordinate-law endpoint — a cleaner shape and a smaller footprint, but not a deletion of the whole stack.

3. Weaker, more honest hypotheses

  • Systematically relaxed [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] → [IsFiniteMeasure μ] wherever μ univ = 1 was unused (TauCeti#723, TauCeti#755, TauCeti#760, TauCeti#790, TauCeti#489).
  • Moved the standard-Borel hypothesis off the sample space onto the value space via condDistrib — [StandardBorelSpace α] not [StandardBorelSpace Ω] (TauCeti#558).

  • Landed the public de Finetti existentials conditionallyIID_of_contractable / conditionallyIID_of_exchangeable on an arbitrary measurable Ω (BlockFactorization.lean:289) — but the directed form conditionallyIIDWith_of_contractable still requires [StandardBorelSpace Ω] (BlockFactorization.lean:269): the arbitrary-Ω upgrade is obtained by path-law transfer for the existential statement, while the concrete directed theorem naming directingProbabilityMeasure μ X remains on the standard-Borel-Ω proof route. (directingProbabilityMeasure itself needs only [StandardBorelSpace α] — it lives over the value space, DirectingMeasure.lean:50; th
    e Ω hypothesis is an artifact of the directed proof route, not of the object.) (TauCeti#824)

  • Stated σ-algebra lemmas with no measure structure at all — omit [MeasurableSpace Ω] (TauCeti#716).

4. Bundle the interface; hide the scaffolding

  • Refined the roadmap's bare existential into the named relation ConditionallyIIDWith + wrapper with destructors (TauCeti#456).
  • Bundled the directing measure as an opaque ProbabilityMeasure-valued directingProbabilityMeasure whose IsProbabilityMeasure instance is automatic, so no measurability hypothesis is needed (TauCeti#564).
  • Kept definitions un-@[expose]d behind characteristic @[simp] lemmas (TauCeti#560) and all rectangle-mixture staging private (TauCeti#824).

5. Prune as you go

Dead scaffolding and dishonest imports were removed rather than carried: futureFiltration (TauCeti#813, TauCeti#822), an unused constant-coordinate product-kernel corollary (TauCeti#835, see the scope example below for the exact declaration), source indicator-product lemmas no longer needed (TauCeti#557), a vestigial case split (TauCeti#621).

[continued]
:robot: drafted with Opus 4.8, revised in light of critique from GPT 5.5

A nice example per rubric

  • reuse — TauCeti#658: the block-product factorisation is obtained from Mathlib's iCondIndepFun characterisation rather than the source's hand-rolled π-system. Runner-up: TauCeti#549 / TauCeti#556 build the shift-invariant and exchangeable σ-algebras on Mathlib's MeasurableSpace.invariants, vendoring nothing; and the whole reverse-martingale layer (TauCeti#685, TauCeti#734, …) is thin adapters over Mathlib's upcrossing/convergence API — "no new martingale theory."

  • proof-quality — TauCeti#617: Contractable.map_single's fin_cases/omega proof that a Fin 1 → ℕ map is StrictMono collapses to h.map (Subsingleton.strictMono k), and map_pair adopts canonical ![i, j] notation. (For the two big cases: TauCeti#567 is a genuine shrinkage — ~46 lines vs the source's 556 + 385-LOC π-system; TauCeti#579 re-routes the directing-measure endpoint through the Mathlib tower rather than shrinking a proof — see §2.)

  • generality — TauCeti#558: reformulating directingMeasure over Mathlib's condDistrib needs only [StandardBorelSpace α], where the source conditioned over Ω and needed [StandardBorelSpace Ω]. Runner-up: TauCeti#824's existential endpoints on arbitrary measurable Ω — with the caveat (§3) that its directed form still needs [StandardBorelSpace Ω].

  • api-design — TauCeti#564: directingProbabilityMeasure bundles the directing measure into the ProbabilityMeasure subtype (instance automatic → no measurability hypothesis), stays opaque, and is exposed only via a @[simp] toMeasure lemma plus a tailProcess-level measurability lemma. Runner-up: TauCeti#456 (ConditionallyIIDWith).

  • correctness — TauCeti#734: the public upcrossings_bdd_uniform was restated on the genuine antitone sequence n ↦ μ[f | 𝔽 n] with the missing Integrable f precondition, fixing an earlier version stated on the reversed surrogate. Companion: TauCeti#743 keeps Integrable f deliberately, so the statement isn't true only via Mathlib's condExp = 0 convention outside L¹.

  • naming — TauCeti#615: renamed the definitional restatements blockLaw_apply / prefixLaw_apply / pathLaw_apply to _def, matching the Mathlib convention and freeing _apply for genuine evaluation lemmas. Companion: TauCeti#755 / TauCeti#825 name the Lévy-downward theorem tendsto_ae_condExp_iInf to mirror Mathlib's forward tendsto_ae_condExp, rather than the roadmap's suggested condExp_tendsto_iInf.

  • placement — TauCeti#775: moved blockIndicatorProd_succ_eq_indicator_inter out of the de-Finetti factorization file into Cylinder.lean beside its Fin 0 companion (and generalised it to an arbitrary selection on the way). Companion: TauCeti#501 / TauCeti#527 put the random-product-kernel lemmas under MeasureTheory/Measure/, not in an exchangeability-specific file.

  • scope — TauCeti#835: removes the unused constant-coordinate corollary aemeasurable_probabilityMeasure_pi_const_toMeasure_of_measurable and switches its call site to the surviving general lemma aemeasurable_probabilityMeasure_pi_toMeasure_of_measurable (ProductKernel.lean:93) — a clean single-topic prune. Companion: TauCeti#464 deliberately defers the conditionally-i.i.d. pushforward case (needs a separate adapter) to keep one topic.

  • documentation — TauCeti#825: fixes a stale docstring in Martingale/Convergence.lean that still referred to the theorem by its old roadmap name, correcting it to the actual tendsto_ae_condExp_iInf — documentation kept honest to the code.

  • attribution — TauCeti#547: rather than silently copying, it records the exact provenance ("adapted from cameronfreer/exchangeability DeFinetti/CommonEnding.lean … to Tau Ceti's current ProbabilityMeasure.pi API"). The discipline is consistent — TauCeti#824 names the source files and the commit pin, and divergence PRs like TauCeti#567 / TauCeti#579 state explicitly how and why they depart from the reference ("strictly more general than the reference").e

Maybe this is better-suited for a discussion elsewhere, but for later reference, here are some of the examples of inter- and intra-rubric conflict that my session mined just now.

:robot: drafted with Opus 4.8, revised in light of critique from GPT 5.5

Rubric conflicts in the TauCeti de Finetti PRs, and how they were resolved

TauCeti PRs are reviewed by ten independent AI agents, one per angle (api-design, attribution, correctness, documentation, generality, naming, placement, proof-quality, reuse, scope). Because each judges in its own lane, two angles sometimes demand incompatible things — or a later review round reverses a change an earlier one required. The contributor guide anticipates this: "If two findings contradict … Contest one of the threads, link the conflicting one, and quote its wording. Show the contradiction; do not just assert one."

I swept the review threads of roughly fifty Exchangeability / de Finetti PRs. 11 PRs carried a genuine conflict (14 instances). The striking pattern: api-design is at the center of nearly every one — it appears in 13 of the 14 instances (colliding with naming 5×, reuse/proof-quality 3×, generality 1×, and itself 4×); the single conflict without api-design is TauCeti#596 (correctness vs generality). Links are Zulip TauCeti#NNN style; quotes are from the review threads.

Pattern 1 — api-design "expose the roadmap's name" vs naming "that name is nonstandard / too generic / overstates"

api-design wants the exact identifier the roadmap advertises to be importable; naming blocks it because the identifier is non-Mathlib-standard, too generic, or promises more than the statement delivers. Naming governed the primary shipped name in every case. But the roadmap README was not rewritten to match — it still carries the planning names (condExp_tendsto_iInf, tailProcess_eq_iInf_revFiltration, shiftInvariantSigma_measurable_shift_eq, deFinetti; that revFiltration is the process-tail spelling, not the later finite-horizon martingale revFiltration in Reverse.lean:46) — and a roadmap-style spelling can survive as an alias beside the conclusion-shaped primary (see counted TauCeti#743, and near-miss TauCeti#734 below). So the rule is "naming wins the primary slot," not "no roadmap name survives."

  • TauCeti#755 — api-design wanted the roadmap handle condExp_tendsto_iInf exposed/importable; naming :no_entry:-blocked it as a nonstandard theorem name. Resolution: renamed to the Mathlib-shaped tendsto_ae_condExp_iInf (mirroring the forward tendsto_ae_condExp), which also serves as the importable handle. Confirmed shipped: Convergence.lean:56 has tendsto_ae_condExp_iInf; condExp_tendsto_iInf appears nowhere in TauCeti/ (though it is still in the roadmap README).
  • TauCeti#824 — api-design asked for a public deFinetti alias; naming required conditionallyIID_of_exchangeable because the eponym overstates a one-directional implication. Resolution: alias removed, conclusion-named theorem kept. Confirmed: no deFinetti theorem exists in TauCeti/; conditionallyIID_of_exchangeable at BlockFactorization.lean:305. Quote: "adding a deFinetti alias would … re-trigger the naming block … the two rubrics cannot both be satisfied by that name."
  • TauCeti#743 — api-design wanted the roadmap's condExp_exists_ae_limit_antitone spelling; naming wanted a conclusion-shaped _of_antitone. Resolution: the primary theorem is exists_integrable_tendsto_ae_condExp_of_antitone, and the roadmap-style spelling survives as an alias beside it (alias condExp_exists_ae_limit_antitone := …, AntitoneLimit.lean:104) — both handles exist, naming governing the primary. Quote: "This is a naming-vs-roadmap-spelling conflict, and I'm siding with the naming rubric … The two can't both be satisfied."
  • TauCeti#549 — api-design demanded exporting the literal roadmap names shiftInvariantSigma_measurable_shift_eq and shiftInvariant_implies_shiftInvariantMeasurable; naming forbids …_eq / …_implies_… on measurability (non-equality) lemmas. Resolution: author contested, api-design withdrew, conclusion-first names kept. Quote: "Both findings cannot hold: naming forbids …_eq / …_implies_… … while this bullet demands exactly those names."
  • TauCeti#526 — naming required dropping the too-generic process-tail revFiltration spelling (around tailProcess_eq_iInf_revFiltration, renamed futureFiltration) while api-design wanted the roadmap-named alias restored. Resolution: futureFiltration kept (naming won); api-design relented. (Note: futureFiltration was itself later deleted as dead code in TauCeti#822 / TauCeti#813 — a separate story.)

Pattern 2 — api-design "make it private" vs reuse / proof-quality "don't duplicate the shared reasoning"

api-design wants a minimal surface (hide helpers); reuse and proof-quality want the shared reasoning available so it isn't duplicated. The concern is duplication, not publicity as such — so it is met by a public helper or a private-but-shared core, depending on where the consumers live. The outcomes here differ precisely on that axis.

  • TauCeti#824 — api-design wanted blockLaw_eq_lintegral_prod_directingMeasure_of_condExp_ae_eq made private; reuse and proof-quality had flagged the ~30-line duplicated integration a shared lemma removes. The author's mid-review contest argued for keeping it public — "is public precisely because two other rubrics required it … making it private re-introduces exactly the ~30-line duplicated integration those rubrics flagged" — but that is not the merged outcome. Final main makes the core private (BlockFactorization.lean:112) and instead colocates both consumers in one file (the iCondIndepFun reduction and the summit), so the duplication is gone with no public helper. Privacy and no-duplication were both satisfied — by consolidation, not by exposing the lemma.
  • TauCeti#755 — proof-quality wanted the generic measurability / L¹ helpers exposed as reusable public lemmas; api-design wanted them private. Here the consumers are genuinely cross-file, so the helpers were extracted into separate merged PRs (TauCeti#687, TauCeti#772 → MeasureTheory/Function/AEStronglyMeasurable.lean and MeasureTheory/Function/ConditionalExpectation.lean, the latter carrying the L¹ conditional-expectation continuity lemma) as public general API, and TauCeti#755 was reduced to consume them — satisfying both.
  • TauCeti#746 — api-design (with proof-quality) wanted public permutation wrappers exists_perm_extending_castLE / exists_perm_nat_extending added; reuse had approved removing those exact wrappers as duplicates of Mathlib's Equiv.Perm.exists_extending_pair. Resolution: reuse won, no wrappers added; api-design narrowed its ask to re-exporting the Mathlib theorem. Quote: "Reintroducing the finite permutation-extension wrappers requested here would knowingly regress the approved reuse rubric. I am therefore not adding those wrappers."

[continued]
:robot: drafted with Opus 4.8, revised in light of critique from GPT 5.5

Pattern 3 — generality "drop the hypothesis" vs correctness / api-design "keep it"

generality flags a hypothesis as unused or too strong; correctness or api-design objects that dropping it makes the statement vacuous or exposes a case the roadmap doesn't want. Resolved not by overruling either, but by refactoring so both are honestly satisfied.

  • TauCeti#734 — generality flagged (hf : Integrable f μ) on exists_lintegral_upcrossings_condExp_le as unused; api-design objected that dropping it exposes a non-integrable case "the roadmap does not need." Resolution: the author restructured the proof so hf.neg is genuinely consumed, keeping hf — now load-bearing rather than unused. Both green. Quotes: generality "dropped … You're right that it's unused"; api-design "the finding stands — exposes a non-integrable case."
  • TauCeti#596 — generality wanted [IsFiniteMeasure μ] removed from integral_blockIndicatorProd as over-strong; correctness hard-blocked the naive removal, because the real identity alone is vacuous at infinite block mass. Resolution: split into three declarations — an honest lintegral_blockCylinder_indicator (ℝ≥0∞, no finiteness), an unconditional integral_blockIndicatorProd (toReal value), and integrable_blockIndicatorProd under [IsFiniteMeasure μ] — so faithfulness lives on the lintegral lemma and generality's target loses the hypothesis. The final three-lemma surface made the unconditional toReal statement acceptable to correctness, and all three went green. Quote: "This is now in direct tension with the other rubrics on the same line … correctness is also green on the current unconditional form."

Pattern 4 — api-design against itself: "remove @[expose]" vs "provide the characteristic _def / _apply lemma"

The most frequent cross-round conflict, entirely within api-design. One round asks for characteristic rewrite lemmas (foo_def, foo_apply) that need the definition body visible; another round asks to remove @[expose], which makes those very lemmas fail to compile. Every time, the author contested with a lake env lean build-error transcript, @[expose] was kept, and the finding was withdrawn — the compiler is the arbiter.

  • TauCeti#451 — remove all @[expose] vs keep the public unfold/simp/eliminator API (blockLaw_def, blockLaw_apply_of_measurable, blockLaw_apply_rectangle, pathLaw_def); not implementable in module mode without dropping the API or adding axioms. Kept @[expose]. Quote: "removing exposure would … drop the named public API … or require axioms/opaque postulates, which would violate the repo axiom-clean rule."
  • TauCeti#526 — remove @[expose] from tailFamily / tailProcess / futureFiltration vs keep exported tailFamily_eq_iSup_comap, futureFiltration_apply. Contested twice ("the finding stands"), then approved with @[expose] kept. (Footnote: the futureFiltration part was kept at merge for this defeq reason but later pruned as dead API in TauCeti#822 / TauCeti#813; tailFamily / tailProcess remain @[expose] on current main, Process/Tail.lean:36.)
  • TauCeti#612 — an earlier round required threeCycleMeasure_def := … rfl; a later round required removing @[expose] from threeCycleMeasure, which breaks that lemma. Contested with a build transcript; api-design withdrew and approved.
  • TauCeti#666 — api-design both lists permReindex_apply as the required characteristic lemma and asks to remove @[expose] from permReindex (which makes permReindex_apply non-defeq and non-building). Author complied with the removable part, contested the rest, kept @[expose].

The resolution playbook

Five mechanisms recur:

  1. Contest-and-link (mandated). The author never silently satisfies one side; they quote the conflicting thread's wording (rubric + round) and show both cannot hold — as the guide requires. Used in every case above.
  2. Naming governs the primary name; the roadmap is a target list, not a naming authority. The primary shipped name follows naming review. The roadmap README is not necessarily edited to match (it still carries the old planning names), and a roadmap-style spelling may be kept as an alias beside the primary (TauCeti#743; near-miss TauCeti#734 has the same alias-survival shape) rather than winning the primary slot.
  3. Sharing constrains privacy — it does not override it. The rule is about duplication, not publicity: if a helper has real cross-file consumers, extract it as public general API (TauCeti#687/#772); if the consumers can be colocated, keep the helper private and share it within the file (TauCeti#824); if it merely duplicates Mathlib, reject the wrapper entirely (TauCeti#746).
  4. Refactor to dissolve, not overrule. The best outcomes (TauCeti#596 split, TauCeti#734 load-bearing hypothesis) satisfy both rubrics by changing the code shape, rather than declaring a winner.
  5. Build error as arbiter. For api-design's internal @[expose]-vs-characteristic-lemma tension, a lake env lean failure transcript is decisive — the compiler settles what taste can't, and @[expose] stays.

Near-misses (checked and rejected as non-conflicts)

  • Agreement, not conflict: TauCeti#658, TauCeti#604 — two angles flagged the same declaration in the same direction.
  • Single-rubric contest: TauCeti#560, TauCeti#579, TauCeti#456 — a finding was contested or complied with, but no opposing rubric required the other side.
  • Single-rubric author contests (rubrics aligned): TauCeti#822, TauCeti#790 — forceful author contests of single findings (a build-breaking import narrowing; a [StandardBorelSpace Ω] drop), where no second rubric opposed. Useful evidence about contested reviews, but not cross-rubric conflicts under the definition used here, so kept out of the headline taxonomy.
  • Same Pattern-1 shape, not separately counted: TauCeti#734's name thread mirrors TauCeti#743 — naming pushed the primary to the Mathlib-shaped exists_lintegral_upcrossings_condExp_le, and the roadmap name upcrossings_bdd_uniform survives as an alias (Bounds.lean:245). Not counted as a separate conflict because no second rubric explicitly required keeping the old primary name (roadmap-target pressure, not an opposing rubric finding); TauCeti#734's one counted conflict is the separate Integrable f hypothesis thread. (If one counts roadmap-target pressure as an opposing angle, this becomes a 15th instance and naming rises to 6×.)
  • Regression caught on re-review: TauCeti#459 — an api-design approve→request_changes flip, but it was a later commit introducing a proof-only public import, fixed without contest — a caught regression, not two contradictory requirements.
  • Satisfiable together: TauCeti#557 — reuse asked to remove a lemma while naming asked to rename it; removal moots the rename, so no irreconcilable clash.
